key_insight: GutCore is a foundation model that can use all stored endoscopy images from a whole exam to assess gastric cancer presence, depth, biomarkers, and prognosis at the patient level.
clinical_relevance: If validated externally, this could help move endoscopic AI from single-frame reading to more complete whole-case decision support for gastric cancer care.
method: Pretrained on 5.6 million de-identified endoscopic images from more than 10 hospitals.
Evaluated on open image-level benchmarks and an internal cohort of 11,035 endoscopic examinations.
Aggregated all exam images for patient-level prediction of cancer status, invasion depth, molecular biomarkers, and survival.
evidence_signal: On the internal cohort, GutCore reached AUC 0.995 for cancer detection, 0.960 for muscularis propria invasion, and 0.804 for SM2-or-deeper invasion, with survival risk groups showing strong separation.
watch_item: Performance was strongest for some biomarkers and lower for HER2, and the authors note that independent clinical validation is still needed before routine use.
paper_title: GutCore: An Endoscopy Foundation Model for Whole-Case Gastric Cancer Analysis
